findings.description: pipeline_list view had no @login_required, unlike sibling leasing_list, causing a 500 (AnonymousUser filter TypeError) instead of a redirect for unauthenticated access
tests/acceptance/test_leasing.py hardcoded a stale route (/leasing/list/) that had never executed under --collect-only

Implemented Phase A of docs/TOP_01_PLAN.md: A-2 (BDD suite over real HTTP via live_server), A-3 (acceptance suite runs pre-merge via live_server fallback), A-4 (real 10-minute build-time budget on docker-publish.yml), A-5 (schema-based response validation for all tests/acceptance/*.py files). A-1 was already done.

pytest-django's static fixturenames-based DB-alias scan never saw tests/acceptance/conftest.py's client->base_url dynamic request.getfixturevalue('db'/'live_server') chain, so migrate never ran and every acceptance request 500'd with 'no such table'

acceptance-check CI job never ran collectstatic, unlike every other test job; masked while the DB bug caused 500s before reaching template rendering, surfaced once that was fixed (ValueError: Missing staticfiles manifest entry)

Self-introduced regression: the pytest_collection_modifyitems hook added to tests/acceptance/conftest.py to fix the DB-alias bug was unscoped, so it mutated fixture markers on ~1600 unrelated tests whenever the Unit Tests CI job collected tests/ as a whole (tests/acceptance/ is a subdirectory), breaking their normal per-test atomic-transaction rollback isolation and causing test_import_csv.py/test_collect_fannie_mae.py failures. Found via full CI log inspection after an initial isolated-file repro wrongly suggested pre-existing flakiness; fixed by filtering items to the conftest's own directory before marking

CI job labeled 'Unit Tests' actually runs ~1600+ tests across nearly the full suite via -k keyword exclusion rather than proper pytest markers/scoping - naming/scope mismatch, out of scope for this repair
